label: refute-t3-products-tychonoff

### FINDING 1 — lem-tube-lemma-for-a-compact-factor — finite basic-box unions always contain a tube
LOCATION: Remarks, line 89
QUOTE: "Compactness of $K$ is essential and cannot be weakened to closedness: the union of finitely many basic boxes over a non-compact $K$ need not contain any tube."
DEFECT: The final clause is false. Any finite union of basic boxes containing the entire slice necessarily contains a tube, regardless of whether K is compact.
EVIDENCE: Write the union as N = ⋃ U_j × V_j and let J consist of those finite indices for which z_0 belongs to V_j. If K is nonempty, J is nonempty. The finite intersection W = ⋂_{j in J} V_j is an open neighbourhood of z_0. For each x in K, some box containing (x,z_0) has its index in J, so every (x,w) with w in W belongs to that same box. Thus K × W is contained in N. The empty K case is immediate with W = Z.
SEVERITY: fatal
MINIMAL REPAIR: Replace "the union of finitely many basic boxes" with "a union of basic boxes".

### FINDING 2 — thm-tychonoff — an arbitrary product-open set can involve infinitely many coordinates
LOCATION: Remarks, line 89
QUOTE: "An arbitrary open cover of $P$ mixes finitely many coordinates in each member and admits no such sorting, which is why the theorem is proved through [[thm-alexander-subbase-lemma]] rather than directly."
DEFECT: The claim about each member is false. Basic open sets restrict finitely many coordinates, but a general open set is an arbitrary union of basic open sets and can depend globally on infinitely many coordinates.
EVIDENCE: Let I be infinite and every factor be the discrete compact space {0,1}. The set O of points having value 1 in at least one coordinate is open because it is the union of the subbasic sets π_i inverse of {1}. It is not determined by any finite coordinate set: for every finite F, the zero vector and a vector supported at one index outside F agree on F, while only the latter lies in O. The set O can, for example, be a member of the open cover {O,P}.
SEVERITY: fatal
MINIMAL REPAIR: Replace the quoted sentence with "Each basic open set restricts only finitely many coordinates, but members of a general open cover may be unions involving different finite coordinate sets and therefore admit no one-coordinate sorting."

### FINDING 3 — cor-heine-borel-in-the-product-topology — the claimed second route still uses bisection
LOCATION: Remarks, line 85
QUOTE: "so [[thm-finite-products-of-compact-spaces]] makes it compact without any appeal to bisection."
DEFECT: The proposed route first obtains compactness of every interval by applying claim 2 with n = 1. Claim 2 comes from thm-heine-borel-rn, whose proof is explicitly the bisection proof. The route reduces the bisection input to one dimension; it does not avoid bisection.
EVIDENCE: The cited target thm-heine-borel-rn says: "The bisection below halves one coordinate at a time and takes the left half whenever the left half still fails to be finitely covered, the right half otherwise."
SEVERITY: fatal
MINIMAL REPAIR: Replace "without any appeal to bisection" with "using only the one-dimensional bisection case".

### FINDING 4 — cor-heine-borel-in-the-product-topology — singleton spaces do not admit metrics of every diameter
LOCATION: Remarks, line 87
QUOTE: "a metrizable space carries metrics of every diameter inducing the same topology."
DEFECT: This universal claim omits a necessary non-singleton hypothesis and does not specify positive finite diameters.
EVIDENCE: On a one-point metrizable space {p}, the metric axiom forces d(p,p) = 0, and there are no other pairs. Its unique compatible metric therefore has diameter 0, so it cannot carry a compatible metric of diameter 1.
SEVERITY: fatal
MINIMAL REPAIR: Replace the quoted clause with "a metrizable space with at least two points carries compatible metrics of any prescribed positive finite diameter."
